_readme: Verification record for every hadith narration cited in data/events. Each entry names the narrator, the wording confirmed at the collection under the number the event cites, and the grading shown on the page. Forty-eight were read at sunnah.com, whose English and Arabic are what the pages show. Two that no sunnah.com collection carries, al-Hakim's Mustadrak 5777 and al-Bayhaqi's Sunan al-Kubra 13211, were read at dorar.net, and their English and French on the pages are renderings made for this project, labelled as such. Narrations in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim are shown as sahih because of the collection they are in; the collections carry no separate grading line for them. npm run verify:citations gates on every citation having an entry and every entry still being cited. It does not judge whether a narration is the right one for its event.

Al-Mustadrak, al-Hakim 5777.confirmedWording: he passed by Ammar and his family while they were being tortured and said, glad tidings, O family of Ammar and family of Yasir, your appointed place is Paradise
Al-Mustadrak, al-Hakim 5777.grade: Sahih on the condition of Muslim (al-Hakim, agreed by adh-Dhahabi)
Al-Mustadrak, al-Hakim 5777.note: Was cited as "Reported in various sources" with no number and the wording "be patient, O family of Yasir". That wording is the popular one; the authenticated wording is "glad tidings". Read at dorar.net (Mustadrak 5777) and hadithanswers.com (Mustadrak 3/388-389). Also in at-Tabarani's al-Awsat 1508, Abu Nu'aym's Ma'rifat as-Sahabah 6664, and al-Bayhaqi's Dala'il an-Nubuwwah 2/282.

As-Sunan al-Kubra, al-Bayhaqi 13211.confirmedWording: I witnessed in the house of Abdullah ibn Jud'an a pact I would not exchange for red camels, and were I called to it in Islam I would answer
As-Sunan al-Kubra, al-Bayhaqi 13211.grade: Chain sahih but mursal, strengthened by corroborating narrations (al-Albani, Fiqh as-Sirah p. 72)
As-Sunan al-Kubra, al-Bayhaqi 13211.note: The collection the event named was right; the narrator and the number were missing. Read at dorar.net, which places it at al-Bayhaqi 13211 and cross-references Ibn Kathir's al-Bidaya 2/293. The clause about returning rights to their owners belongs to al-Humaydi's wording (sahih per Ibn al-Mulaqqin, al-Badr al-Munir 7/325), not to al-Bayhaqi's, so the event no longer states it. The grade was shown as hasan; the record says the chain is sahih but mursal, so the event now shows the mursal grade.

Jami' at-Tirmidhi 324.confirmedWording: prayer in the mosque of Quba is like an Umrah
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 324.note: The number was right; the narrator was recorded as Usaid ibn Hudair, a different companion. The event now shows sunnah.com's English and Arabic in full in place of a project rendering.

Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3620.confirmedWording: the monk recognises the boy by the prostration of rocks and trees and by the seal of prophethood, and says not to take him to Rome because the Romans would recognise him and kill him; the narration does not name Bahira
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3620.note: The earlier wording had the monk warn against the Jews. This narration names the Romans; the Jews appear in Ar-Raheeq al-Makhtum's account instead, and the event now gives both. The block shows sunnah.com's English and Arabic in full. Other gradings are quoted from an answer by Yusuf Shabbir of IslamicPortal.co.uk, republished at islamqa.org/hanafi/islamicportal/117919: al-Baghawi hasan; al-Hakim, al-Jazari and al-Albani sahih; Ibn Hajar judged the chain strong; al-Dhahabi and Shibli Nu'mani doubted the story; the mention of Abu Bakr sending Bilal is held to be an error.

Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3681.confirmedWording: O Allah, honour Islam with the dearer to You of these two men, Abu Jahl or Umar ibn al-Khattab
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3681.note: The event showed a project rendering. It now shows sunnah.com's English and the Arabic of the same narration. The two-groups report in the event is quoted from Ar-Raheeq al-Makhtum, which gives no collection for it; it is listed for scholarly review.

Sahih Muslim 1162b.confirmedWording: asked about fasting on Monday, he said that is the day on which I was born and on which I was commissioned with prophethood or revelation was sent to me
Sahih Muslim 1162b.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 1162b.note: Sahih Muslim 1162 groups several narrations. The stored text came from the one on fasting Arafah and Ashura; the Monday wording is the narration numbered 1162b on sunnah.com, and the event shows it as a marked excerpt.

Sahih Muslim 1218a.narrator: Jabir ibn Abdullah, reported by Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father
Sahih Muslim 1218a.confirmedWording: the Prophet stayed nine years in Madinah without performing Hajj and announced in the tenth year that he was going to perform it, and many people came to Madinah to follow him; the people went to Mina on the day of Tarwiyah and he led five prayers there, then passed on to Arafa where a tent had been pitched for him at Namira; at the bottom of the valley he addressed the people (blood and property sacred, Jahiliyyah practices and blood-revenge abolished beginning with the son of Rabi'a ibn al-Harith, usury abolished beginning with that of Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, fear Allah concerning women, the Book of Allah left among them); the people said they bear witness that he conveyed, fulfilled and advised, and he raised his forefinger to the sky and toward the people and asked Allah three times to be witness; an adhan and then an iqama and the noon prayer, then an iqama and the afternoon prayer with no prayer between; standing facing the qibla until sunset; Muzdalifa, evening and night prayers with one adhan and two iqamas; the dawn prayer and standing at al-Mash'ar al-Haram; pebbles at the jamra; sixty-three camels sacrificed with his own hand and the rest given to Ali, who shared in the sacrifice; Zuhr at Makkah; Zamzam with Banu Abd al-Muttalib
Sahih Muslim 1218a.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 1218a.note: The event shows an excerpt, from Arafa to the Zamzam passage, and replaces the project's earlier English and French, which were worded by the project. The page's English adds Bilal's name in brackets before the adhan; the Arabic gives the verb with no subject, so the event text names Bilal only on Ar-Raheeq's authority. The English adds 'camels' in brackets after sixty-three; a later word in the Arabic (badana) is a camel offered at Hajj, so the event text says camels. The English says a basket where the Arabic says a bucket, and the event text avoids the word. The English 'chastise them but not severely' for the Arabic verb about striking is not relied on in the event text. The page's English has typographical slips ('she pre-Islamic period', 'we are rocks', 'Hadrat 'All') and a footnote number after 'Muhassir', published as is. Ar-Raheeq's longer version of the speech adds further instructions that this narration does not contain, and they are not shown.

Sahih Muslim 1398a.confirmedWording: asked which of the two mosques was founded on piety, the Prophet threw a handful of pebbles on the ground and said it was the mosque in Madinah
Sahih Muslim 1398a.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 1398a.note: Numbered 1398a on sunnah.com. Added so the event shows that the reports differ on which mosque is meant. The event shows sunnah.com English and Arabic in full.

Sahih Muslim 162a.confirmedWording: I was brought al-Buraq, I mounted it and came to Bayt al-Maqdis and tied it to the ring the prophets use
Sahih Muslim 162a.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 162a.note: Replaced Sahih al-Bukhari 349, which is Abu Dharr on the opening of the chest and has no Buraq. The event now shows sunnah.com's English with the Arabic of the same narration in full; the earlier English stopped partway and was a project rendering.

Sahih Muslim 162c.confirmedWording: Jibril came to him while he played with his playmates, opened his breast and took out the blood clot
Sahih Muslim 162c.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 162c.note: Narrowed from Sahih Muslim 162 to the sub-narration that carries this wording. The event now shows sunnah.com's English and Arabic for the whole narration in place of an abridged project rendering.

Sahih Muslim 1763.confirmedWording: a thousand polytheists and 319 Companions at Badr; the Prophet asked Allah to fulfil His promise until his mantle fell and Abu Bakr put it back; a verse was revealed and Allah helped him with angels; seventy killed and seventy captured; Abu Bakr advised ransom, Umar advised execution, the Prophet approved Abu Bakr
Sahih Muslim 1763.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 1763.note: The event now shows sunnah.com's English and Arabic in full in place of a project rendering. The narration runs on through a second chain from Ibn Abbas; the whole narration is shown.

Sahih Muslim 1775a.confirmedWording: Al-Abbas was with the Prophet at Hunayn together with Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith; the Muslims fled when they met the disbelievers while the Prophet spurred his white mule towards them; Al-Abbas held the bridle and Abu Sufyan the stirrup; the Prophet told Al-Abbas, a loud-voiced man, to call the people of as-Samurah, who came back like cows to their calves saying they were present; the call then went to the Ansar and last to Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj; the Prophet threw pebbles in the faces of the disbelievers and said they were defeated by the Lord of Muhammad; the fighting stayed as it was until he threw them, after which Al-Abbas saw their force spent and them retreating
Sahih Muslim 1775a.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 1775a.note: Replaces the project's earlier wording of this narration, which put the line 'I am the Prophet, no lie' in Al-Abbas's account; that line is in 1776a. The page's English has typos ('Abd Sufyan', 'Messenaer', 'may place be upon him') and reads 'people of al-Samura' for the Arabic 'ashab as-samurah'. Ar-Raheeq names the rein-holder only as Abu Sufyan, and its order of rein and stirrup is the reverse of this narration; the event text sets the two side by side.

Sahih Muslim 1776a.confirmedWording: Al-Bara was asked whether they ran away on the Day of Hunayn and said no, by Allah, the Messenger of Allah did not turn his back; young men among his companions went out ahead and met archers of Hawazin and another clan whose arrows rarely missed; they came to the Prophet on his white mule, which Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith was leading; he got down, asked for help, said he was the Prophet and the son of Abd al-Muttalib, and drew up his men
Sahih Muslim 1776a.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 1776a.note: The page's English reads 'Banu Nadir' where the Arabic has 'bani nasr', so the event text names only Hawazin. The Arabic clause on the young men's arms is read by the page's English as 'without any arms or did not have abundant arms'; the event text says only that they went ahead. The Arabic opens with the questioner addressing him as Abu Umarah, the English as Abu Umira.

Sahih Muslim 1780a.confirmedWording: the Prophet advanced until he reached Makkah and sent Zubayr to one flank, Khalid to the other and Abu Ubaydah with the force that had no armour; he said whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe; he went to the Black Stone, circled the Kaaba and, at an idol beside it, pierced its eye with a bow, saying words that match the opening of Quran 17:81; he then went up Safa, raised his hands and praised Allah and prayed
Sahih Muslim 1780a.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 1780a.note: Shown as a marked excerpt, from where the account of the conquest begins to its end. The part left out is the opening frame (Abu Hurairah and the Ansar at Muawiyah's house). The excerpt also reports the Ansar's remark about the Prophet's attachment to his city and his reply, which the event text does not use. sunnah.com's English renders the Arabic 'istalamahu' as 'kissed it'; the event text says only that he went to the Black Stone.

Sahih al-Bukhari 1190.confirmedWording: one prayer in my mosque is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except al-Masjid al-Haram
Sahih al-Bukhari 1190.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 1190.note: The event now shows sunnah.com's English and Arabic in full in place of a project rendering. The published English reads "Al-Masjid-AI-Haram", a misprint, and is kept as published.

Sahih al-Bukhari 1241.confirmedWording: Abu Bakr came on his horse from his home at As-Sunh, entered the Mosque and spoke to no one, went in to Aisha and to the Prophet, who was covered with a marked blanket, uncovered his face, kissed him and wept, and said Allah would not combine two deaths on him and he had died the death written for him; Abu Salama reports from Ibn Abbas that Abu Bakr came out while Umar was speaking to the people, told him to sit and Umar refused, twice, then Abu Bakr said the shahada, the people turned to him, and he said whoever among them worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died, and whoever worshipped Allah, Allah is alive and does not die, and recited 3:144; it was as if the people had not known that Allah revealed the verse until Abu Bakr recited it, and everyone who heard it began reciting it
Sahih al-Bukhari 1241.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 1241.note: The whole narration is shown. It is the entry numbered 1241 and 1242 on the page, and the text is as published there, with Aisha's report of the first part and the report from Abu Salama on the authority of Ibn Abbas joined in one entry. It replaces the project's earlier English and French, which were worded by the project and began Abu Bakr's words with a sentence ('You are dearer to me than my father and mother') that the page does not give in those words. What Umar was saying to the people is not in this narration; the event text takes it from Ar-Raheeq and says so. The page's English renders the shahada as 'the Tashah-hud'; the event text says the shahada.

Sahih al-Bukhari 1586.narrator: Aishah, reported by Yazid ibn Ruman from Urwah
Sahih al-Bukhari 1586.confirmedWording: were your people not close to the Days of Ignorance I would have demolished the Kaaba and rebuilt it on the foundation of Ibrahim
Sahih al-Bukhari 1586.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 1586.note: The event used to show a project rendering whose English said Quraysh 'curtailed its construction', a clause the stored Arabic did not contain. It now shows sunnah.com's English and the Arabic of the same narration as a marked excerpt. The full narration continues with Yazid ibn Ruman's account of Ibn al-Zubayr's rebuilding.

Sahih al-Bukhari 18.confirmedWording: on the night of the Aqaba pledge: swear allegiance to me for not joining anything in worship with Allah, not stealing, not committing adultery
Sahih al-Bukhari 18.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 18.note: Replaced Sahih al-Bukhari 4, which is Jabir on the pause in revelation and carries none of this. The event showed a project rendering that read as a first-person account. It now shows sunnah.com's English with the Arabic of the same passage as a marked excerpt. The narration does not say whether it describes the first or the second night at Aqaba.

Sahih al-Bukhari 2048.confirmedWording: the Prophet made a bond of brotherhood between Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf and Sad ibn ar-Rabi; Sad offered half his wealth and to divorce one of his two wives; Abdur-Rahman declined and asked for the market
Sahih al-Bukhari 2048.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 2048.note: Added to carry the offer of half the wealth and a wife, which the event had stated without a citation. The event shows sunnah.com English and Arabic in full.

Sahih al-Bukhari 2262.confirmedWording: Allah sent no prophet but he shepherded sheep, and I used to shepherd the sheep of the people of Mecca
Sahih al-Bukhari 2262.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 2262.note: The event now shows sunnah.com's English and the Arabic of the same narration in place of a project rendering. The Arabic word is qararit, which sunnah.com's English renders as Qirats. Ibn Hajar (Fath al-Bari on this hadith, shamela.ws/book/1673/2731) reports Suwayd ibn Sa'id's reading as small shares of a dinar or dirham and Ibrahim al-Harbi's as the name of a place in Makkah, and judges the first more likely because Makkans know no such place. The event states both.

Sahih al-Bukhari 2325.confirmedWording: the Ansar asked the Prophet to divide the date palms between them and the Emigrants; he said no; they proposed that the Emigrants look after the trees and share the fruit, and the Emigrants agreed
Sahih al-Bukhari 2325.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 2325.note: Added for the orchards arrangement. The event shows sunnah.com English and Arabic in full.

Sahih al-Bukhari 2617.confirmedWording: a Jewess brought the Prophet a poisoned cooked sheep and he ate from it; she was brought and he was asked whether they should kill her and said no; Anas kept seeing the effect of the poison on the palate of the Prophet's mouth
Sahih al-Bukhari 2617.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 2617.note: The narration does not name Khaybar or give the woman's name; the link to Khaybar and the account of what became of her come from Ar-Raheeq, which says the Prophet ordered her killed after a Companion died of the poison, and the event text sets the two side by side. Replaces the project's earlier claim, with no source, that the poisoning contributed to the Prophet's final illness.

Sahih al-Bukhari 2731.confirmedWording: Suhayl asked for a treaty to be written; he said he did not know al-Rahman and asked for the heading to be by Your name O Allah, which the Prophet had written although the Muslims said they would write nothing else; he refused the wording Messenger of Allah, and the Prophet had Muhammad ibn Abdullah written; he refused entry that year and agreed to the next; he required the return of anyone who came from Quraysh even if Muslim; Abu Jandal arrived in fetters and asked not to be returned to the polytheists; the narration then continues with Umar questioning the Prophet and Abu Bakr, the order to slaughter and shave that the Companions did not obey until Umm Salamah advised the Prophet to do it first, the believing women of 60:10, and Abu Basir
Sahih al-Bukhari 2731.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 2731.note: Shown as a marked excerpt of a long narration, from the arrival of Suhayl to Abu Jandal's plea. The sentences about Umar, Umm Salamah and Abu Basir lie after the excerpt and are given in the prose as Ar-Raheeq's account, with the text noting that al-Bukhari continues. On the English page the excerpt is followed by a site splice marker, and two small typos ("I won't do.:" and a missing closing quotation mark) are sunnah.com's own and are kept. The Arabic chain on the page and the English heading name the narrators as Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwan; the entry shares its page with the next number.

Sahih al-Bukhari 2805.confirmedWording: Anas ibn an-Nadr missed Badr and said Allah would see what he did; at Uhud, when the Muslims broke, he said he found the scent of Paradise before Uhud and went forward; Sad ibn Muadh said he could not do what Anas did; more than eighty wounds were counted on his body and only his sister knew him, by his fingers
Sahih al-Bukhari 2805.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 2805.note: Shown as a marked excerpt ending at the identification by his sister. The rest of the page (the verse thought to be about him, and the case of his sister Ar-Rubayyi breaking a woman's tooth and the retaliation that followed) is a separate matter and is not shown or relied on.

Sahih al-Bukhari 3.confirmedWording: the revelation began with true dreams, then seclusion in the cave of Hira, then the angel saying Read
Sahih al-Bukhari 3.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 3.note: One long narration. Three events quote different parts of it: the beginning of revelation (pre-014), the angel in the cave (mec-001), and Waraqah's answer (mec-002).

Sahih al-Bukhari 3231.confirmedWording: the angel of the mountains offering to close the two mountains of Mecca upon them, and his refusal
Sahih al-Bukhari 3231.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 3231.note: The event showed a project rendering of only the last part of this narration. It now shows sunnah.com's English as a marked excerpt, from the Prophet's answer to Aisha to his reply to the angel, with the Arabic of the same passage. The narration does not name Ta'if; the link to Ta'if is Ar-Raheeq al-Makhtum's.

Sahih al-Bukhari 3653.confirmedWording: Abu Bakr in the cave: if one of them looked under his feet he would see us; the Prophet asked what he thought of two whose third is Allah
Sahih al-Bukhari 3653.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 3653.note: Added so the exchange in the cave rests on the narration where Abu Bakr reports it himself. The event shows sunnah.com English and Arabic in full.

Sahih al-Bukhari 3815.confirmedWording: the best of the world's women is Mary, and the best of the world's women is Khadijah
Sahih al-Bukhari 3815.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 3815.note: Replaced Sahih al-Bukhari 3818, which is Aishah's narration about Khadijah rather than Ali's. The event now shows sunnah.com's English for the Prophet's words, which adds 'at her lifetime' twice in parentheses and ends without a closing quotation mark as published, with the Arabic of the same words. The two isnads on the page are not reproduced.

Sahih al-Bukhari 3816.confirmedWording: I was never as jealous of any wife as of Khadijah, for he mentioned her often, and Allah commanded him to give her good tidings of a palace in Paradise
Sahih al-Bukhari 3816.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 3816.note: The event quoted "she believed in me when people rejected me" under this number. That wording is not Bukhari's; it is Musnad Ahmad 24864, and its grading is disputed (al-Haythami: chain hasan; al-Albani: weak in that complete form, Silsilah Da'ifah 6224). The event now shows sunnah.com's English with the Arabic of the same narration, replacing the earlier project rendering.

Sahih al-Bukhari 3905.confirmedWording: the Prophet told the Muslims he had been shown the land of their migration, a land of date palms between two stony tracts; Abu Bakr waited and fed two she-camels for four months
Sahih al-Bukhari 3905.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 3905.note: The event quoted the exchange in the cave under this number in a project rendering. That exchange is Abu Bakr's own narration, Sahih al-Bukhari 3653, now cited beside it. This number is shown as a marked excerpt on the preparations for the hijrah, with sunnah.com's English.

Sahih al-Bukhari 3906.confirmedWording: the Prophet alighted among Banu Amr ibn Awf on a Monday in Rabi al-Awwal; the mosque founded on piety was established and he prayed in it; his camel then knelt at the drying yard of the orphans Suhayl and Sahl, who offered it as a gift, and he built a mosque there; while building he said that the actual reward is the reward of the Hereafter and asked for mercy on the Ansar and the Emigrants
Sahih al-Bukhari 3906.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 3906.note: Shown as two marked excerpts, one on the stay at Quba and one on the site of the Prophet's Mosque, each with sunnah.com's English and the Arabic of the same passage. The Arabic gives the length of the stay as bid'a 'ashrata laylah, which sunnah.com's English renders as ten nights, so the count is left out of both excerpts and out of the prose.

Sahih al-Bukhari 3934.confirmedWording: the Companions dated the Muslim calendar from the day of the Prophet's arrival in Madinah, not from his mission or his death
Sahih al-Bukhari 3934.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 3934.note: Added to carry the claim that the Hijrah begins the Muslim calendar, which the event had stated without a source. The event shows sunnah.com English and Arabic in full.

Sahih al-Bukhari 3959.confirmedWording: the Companions used to say the men of Badr were three hundred and some ten, the number of the companions of Saul who crossed the river with him
Sahih al-Bukhari 3959.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 3959.note: Added so the event gives both counts of the Badr force (319 in Muslim 1763, over 310 here). The event shows sunnah.com English and Arabic in full.

Sahih al-Bukhari 4.confirmedWording: on the pause in revelation: I saw the angel who came to me in Hira seated between the sky and the earth
Sahih al-Bukhari 4.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih al-Bukhari 4043.confirmedWording: the Prophet placed archers under Abdullah and told them not to leave the place, and not to help if they saw the enemy winning; the Muslims broke the enemy, the archers left for the booty, and seventy were killed; Abu Sufyan asked for Muhammad, Abu Bakr and Umar; the exchange about Hubal and al-Uzza; his remark that the day answered Badr and that some dead would be found mutilated, which he had not ordered and did not regret
Sahih al-Bukhari 4043.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 4043.note: Shown as a marked excerpt. The page goes on to a separate report from Jabir about men who drank wine on the morning of Uhud and were killed as martyrs; it is not shown or relied on. The English adds the words (at a special place), (of the battle of Uhud) and (to) in parentheses that the Arabic does not carry.

Sahih al-Bukhari 4098.confirmedWording: we were with him at the Trench carrying earth on our shoulders, and he said there is no life but the life of the Hereafter
Sahih al-Bukhari 4098.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 4098.note: Replaced Sahih al-Bukhari 4109, which is Sulayman ibn Surad and carries different wording. The event now shows sunnah.com's English and Arabic in full in place of a project rendering.

Sahih al-Bukhari 4110.confirmedWording: when the clans were driven away the Prophet said that from now on the Muslims would go out against them and they would not go out against the Muslims, and that the Muslims would march to them
Sahih al-Bukhari 4110.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 4110.note: Added so the event can state the Prophet's words after the siege from a collection instead of from memory. The page spells the narrator Sulaiman bin Surd; the Arabic reads Sulayman ibn Surad.

Sahih al-Bukhari 4154.confirmedWording: on the day of Hudaybiyah the Prophet said to the Companions that they were the best people on the earth; Jabir says they were 1400, and that if he could see he would show the place of the tree; the page adds that Salim said the number was 1400
Sahih al-Bukhari 4154.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 4154.note: Shown as a marked excerpt that ends before the closing remark that Salim gave the same number. The English adds the words (beneath which we gave the Pledge of Allegiance), which are not in the Arabic and are not relied on.

Sahih al-Bukhari 4210.confirmedWording: on the day of Khaybar the Prophet said he would give the flag the next day to a man through whose hands Allah will give victory, who loves Allah and His Messenger and is loved by them; Ali, who had eye trouble, was sent for, the Prophet spat in his eye and prayed for him and he was cured, and was given the flag; the Prophet told him to proceed without hurrying, call them to Islam and tell them of Allah's right which they should observe, and that if Allah guides one man through him that is better for him than the nice red camels
Sahih al-Bukhari 4210.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 4210.note: Replaces the project's earlier English and French, which were worded by the project. The page's English reads 'give us victory'; the Arabic has no word for 'us' and the event text does not rely on it. Ali's words about fighting them are a statement in the English and a question in the Arabic, so the event text speaks only of him asking about fighting them.

Sahih al-Bukhari 428.confirmedWording: the Prophet stayed fourteen nights among Banu Amr ibn Awf; he asked the Banu an-Najjar to name a price for their walled plot and they said they would ask its price only from Allah; graves, ruins and palms were cleared
Sahih al-Bukhari 428.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 428.note: Added because it gives a length of stay and an owner of the land that differ from the other reports. Shown as two marked excerpts with sunnah.com's English and the Arabic of the same passages.

Sahih al-Bukhari 4287.confirmedWording: on the day of the conquest there were 360 idols around the Kaaba and the Prophet struck them with a stick in his hand, saying words that open like Quran 17:81 and end like Quran 34:49
Sahih al-Bukhari 4287.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 4287.note: Replaces the project's earlier English, which ended the saying with the end of Quran 17:81 and said he destroyed the idols; the Arabic ends with the words of 34:49. sunnah.com's English leaves out the Arabic's 'and falsehood has perished, truth has come' before 'and falsehood will neither start nor reappear', and renders yat'unuha (poked or stabbed) as 'striking'. The event text relies on the Arabic for the match with Quran 17:81 and 34:49.

Sahih al-Bukhari 4418.confirmedWording: Ka'b says the Prophet hid his intention on expeditions until Tabuk, which he fought in severe heat with a long journey, desert and many enemies, and he told the Muslims plainly where he was going; the Prophet asked about Ka'b at Tabuk and a man of Banu Salama said his two garments and his pride had kept him back, which Mu'adh ibn Jabal rejected; on the Prophet's return something over eighty men came with excuses and oaths and he accepted the excuses they had expressed, took their pledge, asked forgiveness for them and left their hearts to Allah; Ka'b said he had no excuse and had never been stronger or wealthier, the Prophet said he had spoken the truth and told him to get up until Allah decided his case; the Muslims were forbidden to speak to Ka'b, Murara ibn ar-Rabi and Hilal ibn Umayya, and this lasted fifty nights
Sahih al-Bukhari 4418.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 4418.note: The event shows an excerpt of the narration, from the Prophet's habit of hiding his destination to the end of the first fifty nights, and replaces the project's earlier English, which was worded by the project. The narration continues with the end of the boycott, the announcement of Allah's acceptance of their repentance and Ka'b's reply on giving away his wealth; the event text does not rely on that part. The page's English glosses the man's words as 'his two Burdas (i.e. garments) and his looking at his own flanks with pride'; the event text says only that his two garments and his pride had kept him back.

Sahih al-Bukhari 4449.confirmedWording: Aisha says it was among Allah's favours to her that the Prophet died in her house on the day of her turn, leaning against her chest, and that Allah mixed her saliva with his at his death; Abd ar-Rahman came in with a siwak, she saw him looking at it and softened it for him at his nod, and he cleaned his teeth with it; in front of him was a jug or a tin of water, in which he dipped his hand(s) and rubbed his face, saying there is no god but Allah and death has its agonies; he then raised his hand and kept saying words about the highest companion until he died and his hand dropped
Sahih al-Bukhari 4449.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 4449.note: The whole narration is shown, and it replaces the project's earlier English and French, which were worded by the project and repeated the words about the highest companion that the narration gives once. The page's English says the Prophet was leaning against her chest; the Arabic says between her sahr and her nahr, and the event text follows the English. The English says 'his hand' where the Arabic has both hands going into the water, and 'lifted his hands' where the Arabic has one hand raised, so the event text says only that he wiped his face with water and does not say how many hands. The jug-or-tin doubt belongs to the sub-narrator Umar ibn Said, and the event text says jug. The page's English renders the name of Abd ar-Rahman with a backtick as 'Abdur-Rahman', published as is.

Sahih al-Bukhari 4486.confirmedWording: the Prophet prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen or seventeen months while wishing for the Kaaba; an Asr prayer facing the Kaaba; a man told people bowing in another mosque and they turned; men killed before the change and the verse revealed about them
Sahih al-Bukhari 4486.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 4486.note: The event now shows sunnah.com's English and Arabic in full in place of a project rendering. The English adds (2.144) and (2.143) and the words "in his Mosque" in parentheses; the Arabic carries none of the three, so the prose does not rely on them.

Sahih al-Bukhari 4770.confirmedWording: when warn your closest kindred was revealed he ascended Safa and called O Bani Fihr, O Bani Adi
Sahih al-Bukhari 4770.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 4770.note: The event showed a project rendering that gave only part of this narration. It now shows sunnah.com's English and the Arabic of the same narration in full. The Quran verses it mentions are 26:214 and 111:1-5.

Sahih al-Bukhari 604.confirmedWording: the Muslims at Madinah guessed the time of prayer; a bell and a horn were suggested; Umar was the first to suggest that a man call; the Prophet ordered Bilal to call
Sahih al-Bukhari 604.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 604.note: Added so the account of how the adhan began rests on the narration that gives the discussion and the proposals. The event shows sunnah.com English and Arabic in full.

Sahih al-Bukhari 64.confirmedWording: the Prophet sent his letter with a man to the governor of Bahrain, who sent it to Khosrau; when he read it he tore it to pieces; the sub-narrator Ibn Shihab thinks Ibn al-Musayyab said that the Prophet invoked Allah against them that they be torn to pieces
Sahih al-Bukhari 64.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 64.note: Replaces the project's earlier saying attributed to the Prophet about Khosrau's kingdom, which no collection page read this session gives. The invocation in this narration is reported with doubt by the sub-narrator, and the event text says so. The English page names the ruler Chousroes; the Arabic reads Kisra.

Sahih al-Bukhari 7.confirmedWording: Abu Sufyan, with a Quraysh caravan in Ash-Sham during the truce, was summoned by Heraclius at Ilya and questioned about the Prophet; Heraclius said that if what Abu Sufyan had said was true the Prophet would soon occupy the place beneath his feet, that he knew a prophet was to appear but did not think he would be from among them, and that he would wash his feet; the letter of the Prophet, brought by Dihya to the governor of Busra and passed to Heraclius, was read, followed by a great hue and cry and the removal of Abu Sufyan and his companions; the narration then continues with Ibn an-Natur's report of Heraclius at Ilya and Homs, his calling the Byzantines to pledge to the Prophet, their running to the doors, and his saying he had spoken to test their conviction
Sahih al-Bukhari 7.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih al-Bukhari 7.note: Shown as a marked excerpt, from Heraclius's reply to the end of Abu Sufyan's account. The English adds the words (the Prophet (ﷺ) Muhammad) and (Byzantine), and 'Ibn-Abi-Kabsha)' carries a stray bracket; these are sunnah.com's own. The part after the excerpt, Ibn an-Natur's report about Heraclius at Ilya and Homs, is not shown or relied on in the event text.

Sunan Abu Dawud 499.confirmedWording: the dream of the man carrying a bell, and the words of the adhan he was taught
Sunan Abu Dawud 499.note: Replaced Sunan Abi Dawud 498, which is Abu Umayr ibn Anas on how the people were gathered. The event now shows sunnah.com's English and Arabic as a marked excerpt in place of a project rendering. The English gives Bilal's louder voice as the reason he should call; the Arabic word is andā, which the event leaves out rather than choose between the two readings.

Sunan Ibn Majah 150.confirmedWording: the first to declare their Islam were seven: the Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr, Ammar and his mother Sumayyah, Suhayb, Bilal and Miqdad; the idolaters put the others in coats of chain mail and left them in the sun, and Bilal alone did not give in, and was handed to the children who led him through the streets of Makkah while he said Ahad, Ahad
Sunan Ibn Majah 150.note: Added to the event so the Bilal detail rests on a collection and not on a project rendering. The event shows sunnah.com English and Arabic in full.
